issues.details: Homepage blocked by WAF/security challenge - content not accessible to agents
issues.name: Content without JavaScript
issues.recommendation: Serve at least 500 characters of meaningful homepage content in raw HTML. Add a clear H1, keep deeper heading levels sequential, and remove excessive non-content markup. Inner pages need their main text in the raw HTML too, not only after JavaScript runs.

issues.details: Bot management challenged ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot. A challenge is an identity check that verified crawlers pass, so this is not proof agents are blocked - but unverified agents will not get through.
issues.name: Not blocked by bot detection
issues.recommendation: Verify that major agent User-Agents can reach the homepage. If your WAF or bot rules block them, remove or narrow the blocking rule. Add an allow rule only when your security setup denies them by default.

issues.name: OpenAPI spec published
issues.recommendation: Publish an OpenAPI (Swagger) specification at /openapi.json or /api/openapi.yaml. This is how agents understand your API surface automatically.

issues.details: API does not return JSON error responses (or no API detected)
issues.name: JSON error responses
issues.recommendation: Return structured JSON error responses with error codes, messages, and resolution hints. Agents can't parse HTML error pages.

issues.details: Homepage https://lehamim.co.il does not meet the Markdown negotiation requirements: Accept: text/markdown returned text/html; Vary header missing Accept (got "none")
issues.name: Markdown content negotiation (acceptmarkdown.com)
issues.recommendation: Enable Markdown negotiation on the scanned homepage. Supporting it only on /docs or a separate .md URL does not satisfy this check. Requests with Accept: text/markdown must receive a nonempty Markdown body with Content-Type: text/markdown and Vary: Accept. Keep serving HTML for Accept: text/html. Adding Vary alone does not create a Markdown response. Verify both with `curl -sS -L -i -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://yourdomain.com/` and `curl -sS -L -i -H 'Accept: text/html' https://yourdomain.com/`. Check the final response headers and body: Markdown with Vary: Accept for the first request, HTML for the second.

issues.details: In a search for your API docs, none of the 10 results is your official docs
issues.name: Developer resource discoverability
issues.recommendation: Make sure a web search for your product's API docs returns your own docs page, and a search for your MCP server, SDK or CLI returns your own pages for those tools. Keep docs on your own domain or a subdomain, or link your docs site from your homepage or llms.txt, give each tool its own page (for example /mcp) with the tool name in the title, put your product name and "API" in the docs title and main heading, and link your GitHub org from your homepage.

issues.name: Developer portal
issues.recommendation: Create a developer portal at /developers with API keys, documentation, quickstart guides, and a sandbox environment.

issues.details: Homepage blocked by WAF - cannot check structured data
issues.name: JSON-LD structured data
issues.recommendation: Add JSON-LD structured data to your homepage using the identity type that matches your site - SoftwareApplication for products, Organization or LocalBusiness for companies, Person for personal sites, Article for blogs - with name, description, url, and type-appropriate fields (offers, sameAs, author) so AI can parse your identity programmatically.

issues.name: CLI tool available
issues.recommendation: Publish an official CLI tool on npm, PyPI, or Homebrew. A CLI lets agents and developers script interactions with your product without building API integrations from scratch.

issues.details: Homepage blocked by WAF - cannot check for docs links
issues.name: Public API/docs linked from homepage
issues.recommendation: Publish API documentation at a discoverable URL (/docs, /api, /developers). Include authentication, endpoints, and example requests.

issues.details: No agent instruction file with when-to-use guidance found
issues.name: Agent instruction / when-to-use
issues.recommendation: Tell agents when to reach for you: add a 'when to use this' section to your llms.txt (or a dedicated agent-instructions file) that names your best-fit use cases and how an agent should call you. Be specific about the jobs you are right for - generic marketing copy does not read as guidance.

issues.details: GraphQL introspection auth-gated and no header convention documented on GraphQL-tagged pages
issues.name: Rate limit response headers
issues.recommendation: Return standard rate-limit headers on your API responses (the RFC RateLimit headers, plus Retry-After on a 429) so agents can self-throttle in real time, and document the conventions alongside your API.

issues.details: GraphQL: introspection auth-gated and no schema evidence in docs
issues.name: API schema complexity analysis
issues.recommendation: Make your API spec self-describing: a unique operationId and a description on every operation, typed parameters, and response schemas. For GraphQL, a fully typed schema with a documented cost or rate limit reads best.

issues.details: No API spec found - function calling requires discoverable endpoints
issues.name: Function calling compatibility
issues.recommendation: Ensure API endpoints have unique operation IDs, typed schemas, and descriptions compatible with LLM function-calling formats.

issues.name: Sitemap exists
issues.recommendation: Add a valid XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml listing all indexable URLs. Include lastmod dates and keep it under 50MB.

issues.details: Homepage blocked by WAF - cannot check metadata
issues.name: Metadata completeness
issues.recommendation: Add all four signals to your homepage: <link rel="canonical"> pointing to the page on your own site, <html lang="...">, <meta property="og:image">, and <meta property="og:type">. Agents use these for entity resolution and attribution.

issues.details: Homepage blocked by WAF - cannot check Organization schema
issues.name: Organization schema completeness
issues.recommendation: Add Organization JSON-LD that includes both contactPoint (with email/phone and contactType) and address (PostalAddress). This lets AI verify your business legitimacy and answer contact queries.

issues.details: No trust anchor pages found with sufficient content (About, Contact, Privacy)
issues.name: Trust anchor pages
issues.recommendation: Publish real /about, /contact, and /privacy pages with at least 500 characters of content each. These are the pages AI agents check to verify your business is legitimate before recommending you.

issues.details: lehamim.co.il ranks #10 for "lehamim.co.il" (searched your brand name alone: we could not read a product term from your site)
issues.name: Brand name discoverability
issues.recommendation: Make sure your own domain ranks in the top results when people search your brand together with your main product (for example "Acme payments API"). Ora first reads product terms from your homepage's JSON-LD keywords or knowsAbout, or its meta keywords tag. If none qualifies, it checks the main service's serviceType in JSON-LD, then a short product phrase in the page title. If those do not qualify, it checks product names in the homepage business's JSON-LD offers. Use clear product terms that also appear on the page. If no term qualifies, Ora searches your brand name alone. If your domain does not rank, your brand may be too generic, conflict with a more established term, or not yet indexed. Strengthen it by describing your main product clearly in your homepage title and headings, earning press mentions that link to your domain, and avoiding redirect chains that mask your main domain in search results.
